gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the "0.125 ms" latency makers print for these boards is just the 8,000 Hz report interval (1 ÷ 8,000 s), while the only measured figures in the under-$100 TMR group are four to six times that and nearly level: 0.60 ms wired / 0.75 ms 2.4 GHz for the Gamakay TK75 TMR (HLPlanet, OSLTT) against about 0.5-0.6 ms wired for the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR, with no measurement at all for the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide (cited), PCWorld (cited), Notebookcheck (cited), keyboardtester.click (cited), GamePadSquire's FUN60 Ultra TMR review and HLPlanet's TMR-vs-Hall page (both in the results, uncited); RTINGS' 60% list rendered empty for me, so I could not compare its body text. mkbguide gives per-mode polling for the HE65 V2 TMR (8,000 / 8,000 / 125 Hz) but no latency, rapid-trigger step, scan rate or battery, and says only that polling is not a latency measurement. keyboardtester.click gives the TK75 TMR's 256 kHz scan rate and 8,000 mAh battery but no latency figure for any board, and prices it at $109.99. GamePadSquire carries measured latency and battery hours for the FUN60 alone. None puts the three boards on one basis, none has HLPlanet's TK75 TMR measurement or its roughly 0.3 mm phantom-release finding, none flags that the FUN60's 3 h and the HE65's 30 h battery figures were taken at different polling rates, and none carries MonsGeek's own footnote that 0.01 mm is guaranteed only on six listed switches. It is not a 3 because GamePadSquire already has the FUN60 half of the latency comparison.
decides: Latency does not separate the boards: the TK75 TMR's measured 0.60 ms wired sits level with the FUN60 Ultra TMR's roughly 0.5-0.6 ms, and all three advertise the same 8,000 Hz and 0.01 mm. The pick therefore falls to layout, battery, Bluetooth rate and price. The Gamakay TK75 TMR (ours, $89.99 at the sale price only; list $159.99) is an honest pick for the 75% / long-battery segment: 8,000 mAh against 4,000 mAh, Bluetooth at 1,000 Hz against the HE65's 125 Hz, and it is one of the two boards with a measured latency. The Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR at $59.99 wins on price and arrow keys but has an ABS case and no measured latency. The FUN60 Ultra TMR keeps the aluminium 60% slot, with about 3 h at 8K wireless and a polling rate the driver cannot lower (Notebookcheck). The caveat for our row is to set rapid-trigger release near 0.4 mm, not 0.01 mm (HLPlanet). Womier's K75 TMR, which ChatGPT showed at $85.99 from Newegg, is $119.99 at Womier's own store today, so it is over the line there.

findings.label: What the makers' "0.125 ms" figure is
findings.value: 0.125 ms = 1 ÷ 8,000 Hz, the interval between USB reports, not key-to-PC latency
findings.source_title: EPOMAKER HE80 (Epomaker US store listing text, read through store search)
findings.note: Epomaker's own HE80 copy ties the figure to polling: "latency is significantly reduced to a mere 0.125ms, 8x quicker than conventional 1k polling keyboard". Its HE68 Lite copy says 8 kHz polling registers "in 0.125 millisecond". Arithmetic: 1 / 8,000 s = 0.000125 s = 0.125 ms; 1 / 1,000 s = 1 ms, which is the 8x.

findings.label: Maker latency claim per mode, and whether anyone measured it
findings.value: 0.125 ms wired, 0.125 ms 2.4 GHz, 14 ms Bluetooth (maker claim as quoted by HLPlanet); no measured latency in the review
findings.source_title: Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR Review (HLPlanet, dated 2026-09-07)
findings.note: HLPlanet reports the maker's figures and says the reviewer could not perceive a difference between 0.125 ms and a few milliseconds; no test tool is named. I could not open Epomaker's own product page (HTTP 429), so the claim is read from the reviewer's page.

findings.label: Measured latency (named reviewer)
findings.note: HLPlanet measured with OSLTT. Arithmetic: 0.60 / 0.125 = 4.8x and 0.75 / 0.125 = 6.0x the 8,000 Hz report interval. HLPlanet reviewed it at $119.99, with Mercury V3 switches.

findings.label: Measured latency (secondhand)
findings.value: RTINGS about 0.5 ms single-key and about 0.7 ms multi-key; IGN about 0.6 ms wired and about 1.1 ms 2.4 GHz
findings.source_title: MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR Review (GamePadSquire, dated 2026-08-01)
findings.note: Read on GamePadSquire, which attributes the figures to RTINGS and IGN. RTINGS' own review page returned no body text to me, so these are not verified at the original source. Different rigs from HLPlanet's OSLTT, so compare the TK75 TMR figure only loosely.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection, scan rate
findings.value: 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth; 256,000 Hz scan rate
findings.note: Gamakay's own blog post (https://gamakay.com/blogs/news/gamakay-tk75-tmr-review-budget-tmr-keyboard-iso-de, read 2026-11-26) states 8,000 Hz for wired and 2.4 GHz and gives no Bluetooth rate.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection, scan rate, build
findings.value: 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 125 Hz Bluetooth; 64,000 Hz scan rate; ABS plastic case; 66 keys plus a knob
findings.note: mkbguide (https://mkbguide.com/blog/best-gaming-keyboards-under-100, read 2026-11-26) gives the same 8,000 / 8,000 / 125 Hz split as Epomaker's listing. Scan rate is 64 kHz against the TK75 TMR's 256 kHz, both from HLPlanet's spec lists.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection (maker)
findings.value: 8,000 Hz in wired or 2.4 GHz modes; no Bluetooth rate and no scan rate stated
findings.note: Page wording: "8000Hz polling rate in wired or 2.4G wireless modes". Battery is listed as "4000mAh (for tri-mode version only)".

findings.label: Rapid-trigger "0.01 mm" as the maker qualifies it
findings.value: RT range 0.01-2.00 mm, actuation 0.1-3.40 mm; 0.01 mm precision guaranteed only for six listed switches, other switches may perform at 0.1 mm
findings.note: Mechanical-switch support is for the TMR version only. The page says Akko Magnetic Creamy Yellow switches are not compatible because of magnet orientation.

findings.label: Rapid-trigger usable floor against the advertised step
findings.value: Adjustable to 0.01 mm; phantom releases on neighbouring keys at release settings below about 0.3 mm; reviewer suggests about 0.4 mm
findings.note: HLPlanet attributes it to plate flex under firm presses and gives no confirmed phantom-free minimum. It also advises turning rapid trigger off on any key fitted with a mechanical switch.

findings.label: Battery life and the polling rate it was measured at
findings.value: 4,000 mAh; about 3 h on 2.4 GHz at 8,000 Hz with LEDs on; about 4-5 h on Bluetooth
findings.source_title: MonsGeek Fun60 Ultra TMR hands-on review (Notebookcheck, dated 2025-03-30)
findings.note: Notebookcheck says the driver cannot change the polling rate, so runtime cannot be traded for speed. PCWorld (https://www.pcworld.com/article/3014690/monsgeek-fun60-ultra-review.html, read 2026-11-26) says it "often only lasted a few hours" at 8,000 Hz with RGB on and that the mode switch sits under the Caps Lock keycap.

findings.label: Battery life and the polling rate it was measured at
findings.value: 4,000 mAh (2 × 2,000 mAh); about 30 h with RGB on
findings.note: HLPlanet used 1,000 Hz for daily testing, so the 30 h is not comparable with the FUN60's 3 h at 8,000 Hz. Both are 4,000 mAh. Brightness and usage pattern are not specified.

findings.label: Battery
findings.value: 8,000 mAh; not depleted during HLPlanet's review period
findings.note: Twice the capacity of the FUN60 Ultra TMR and HE65 V2 TMR (4,000 mAh each). No hour figure exists.
